test_title: PYST 16: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 12 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A tap fills a cistern in 14 hours. Another tap empties the full tank in 18 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill the tank completely, if the tank is empty and both the taps are open together?
solution:
**Given:**

Filling tap time = 14 hours

Emptying tap time = 18 hours

**Formula used:**

LCM method: Take LCM of both times to assume total work (litres)

Then: Work done per hour = Filling - Emptying

Time = Total work ÷ Net work per hour

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM of 14 and 18 = 126 litres (assume total capacity)

⇒ Filling rate = 126 ÷ 14 = 9 litres/hour

⇒ Emptying rate = 126 ÷ 18 = 7 litres/hour

⇒ Net rate = 9 − 7 = 2 litres/hour

⇒ Time = 126 ÷ 2 = 63 hours

**∴ The tank will be filled completely in 63 hours.**
